title: Benchmark-lab: run kernel selector v2 experiments across GPU matrix + prompt distributions; publish report artifact
creator: Rina Kobayashi
description:
Goal
Update benchmark-lab so we can run A/B experiments for kernel selector v2 vs v1 across a representative GPU matrix and prompt distributions (prefill vs decode, short vs long context), then publish a report artifact that can be used for:
- perf-canary gating inputs (ENG-3930)
- rollout decision-making (ENG-3934)
- regression triage (SRE + runtime)

Scope
1) Experiment harness changes
- Add selector toggle: selector_version={v1|v2} (plumbed into runtime config for the benchmark job).
- Add explicit capture of selector context fields in outputs: model_family, seq_bucket, gpu_sku_normalized, selected_kernel_id.
- Ensure deterministic run mode for comparisons: pinned model revision, pinned runtime build, fixed seeds where applicable.

2) GPU matrix
Target SKUs (initial): L4, A10, A100-80G, H100 (SXM where available). If we can only get PCIe H100 in the lab, document and keep as separate series.

3) Model + prompt set
Models (initial):
- Llama-family: 8B/70B equivalent (whatever is in our internal catalog for benchmark-lab)
- Mistral-family: 7B/8x7B equivalent
- Qwen-family: 7B/14B equivalent

Prompt distributions (per model):
- Short prefill: prompt_len bucket ~[0-256], target gen_len ~[64-128]
- Medium: prompt_len ~[256-1024], gen_len ~[128-256]
- Long-context: prompt_len ~[4k-16k], gen_len ~[256] (enough decode to capture steady-state)
- Decode-heavy: prompt_len ~[256-1k], gen_len ~[1k-2k]

Note: Use the same distribution buckets as selector v2’s seq buckets (from scheduler signal) to avoid mismatch between selection logic and benchmark labels.

4) Metrics + reporting
Collect and publish:
- Latency: p50/p90/p95 end-to-end; and component if available (prefill time, decode tok/s)
- Throughput: tokens/sec and requests/sec where applicable
- Cost proxy: ms/token and tok/s per GPU (we don’t need $ until later, but include enough to estimate)
- Stability: variance across runs; outliers list
- Correctness checks: basic output sanity (no NaNs, no crashes); conformance tests handled in ENG-3928 but benchmark should flag any runtime errors.

Report artifact
- Single rollup table per model family: GPU x seq_bucket with v1 vs v2 deltas.
- Include a short narrative section: ‘wins’, ‘regressions’, suspected causes, and recommended selector registry follow-ups.
- Store artifact in the standard benchmark-lab location and link from Confluence benchmark plan + runtime weekly notes.

Acceptance criteria
- One command (or CI workflow) can run v1 and v2 back-to-back with same matrix definition.
- Output includes selector decision metadata so we can correlate performance with kernel_choice.
- Report artifact generated automatically and attached to benchmark run, with stable filenames and timestamps.
- Baseline coverage: at least 3 model families x 3 seq buckets x 3 GPU types (minimum) before we call this ‘complete’; the full desired matrix is 4x4x4 but may be constrained by hardware availability.

Out of scope
- Defining perf gate thresholds (ENG-3930)
- Writing new kernels or changing kernel implementations

Links
- GitHub: benchmark-lab/pr_941_selector_v2_benchmark_matrix
- Confluence: kernel-selector-v2 benchmark plan (owned by Claire Dubois)

Open questions
- Do we need to split H100 PCIe vs SXM in reporting? (likely yes)
- How do we represent MIG/partitioned GPUs in benchmark-lab labels without exploding cardinality? (prefer ‘gpu_partition=none|mig’ and keep details in run metadata)

Risks
- Hardware availability (A10 capacity in lab has been flaky). If we can’t run full sweeps, prioritize L4 + A100 + H100 and include A10 as best-effort.
- Cardinality: capturing per-request kernel id might blow up report size. Solution: aggregate by (gpu_sku, model_family, seq_bucket, selector_version) and keep raw samples behind a separate flag.
comments: 2026-01-22 (Rina Kobayashi): Put up initial PR to add matrix definition for selector_version A/B + GPU SKU normalization in the benchmark metadata. Waiting on final field names from ENG-3927 telemetry spec to keep consistency. PR: benchmark-lab/pr_941_selector_v2_benchmark_matrix

2026-01-28 (Claire Dubois): Please ensure the prompt distributions match the buckets we use for rollout SLO review (short, medium, long-context, decode-heavy). Also add a note on how many iterations per cell so p95 is meaningful (recommend >= 200 samples per cell where feasible).

2026-02-03 (Sana Farid): For variance, we should run each cell at least 3 times and report min/median/max p95 to catch noisy regressions. If too expensive, at least do this for long-context buckets on A10 and L4.

2026-02-08 (Yuki Sato): GPU SKU normalization: please log both raw CUDA name and normalized sku so we can catch mis-detections (esp. A10 variants). Keep normalized sku as the primary grouping key in the report.

2026-02-12 (Rina Kobayashi): Added selector_version toggle plumbing in benchmark job config and captured selected_kernel_id + seq_bucket in the result rows. Report generator now produces a single HTML + CSV bundle per run with a stable naming convention (run_id + git SHA).

2026-02-18 (Marcus Reed): Ran an initial sweep for L4/A100/H100 on Llama-family and Mistral-family. Looks consistent with local perf smoke tests. One anomaly: A10 long-context p95 regressed in v2 by ~8–12% in 2/3 runs; tagging runtime team to cross-check against known A10 issue thread and confirm seq_bucket boundaries are correct.

2026-02-21 (Rina Kobayashi): Requested review. Remaining item: document how to interpret the rollup table and where to find raw samples; also add guardrails so failures (OOM/crash) are surfaced as explicit ‘error’ cells in the report instead of missing data.
